answer: Each voting seat is a one-key compute quota sold in a standing auction and paid in jade; after the bid clears, the winner must finish a live challenge that cannot be precomputed or reused. Quotas do not split, so cloning a key simply voids the seat. At every tide change the protocol compares funding graphs and solution fingerprints; matching clusters are marked sable and their payments are burned. An attacker who wants a thousand votes must win a thousand auctions, solve a thousand live challenges, and still risk losing the entire spend if those keys are clustered.
